A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MindForge work and contain 30 readable pages. The main text, figures, tables, Appendices A-G and checklist can be reliably matched despite reordered back matter.

before.justification: V5 reports original Minecraft experiments measuring task success, tech-tree progression, collaboration and generalization, with additional experiments and ablations in Appendices A-B.

after.justification: V6 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices A-B, including the task-success and tech-tree results in Tables 1-9.

M1.justification: Section 4 and the implementation appendices retain the same structured beliefs, perspective-taking procedure, communication mechanism and episodic, semantic and procedural memory components.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Minecraft tasks, tech-tree evaluations, human/expert and peer collaboration scenarios, and post-collaboration/OOD tests. Execution-log and Minecraft documentation sources for fine-tuning are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Voyager variants, PEFT-tuned Mistral-7B, Table 3's ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT, and Table 8's Think Twice-inspired unstructured alternative.

E3.justification: Both retain the same model configurations, four-action base protocol, communication conditions and tech-tree evaluation procedure. Task-success, milestone and unique-item metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The communication-round analyses, alternative communication protocol, post-collaboration/OOD tests, perspective-taking and memory ablations, and qualitative failure examples are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report 24 independent task trials and three tech-tree trials, with identical uncertainty reporting in Table 3. No run-count, seed, interval or significance-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1's Mistral-7B MindForge scores remain 37.5% for dirt and 33.3% for wood.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. The BigToM/BDI conceptual account and Section 5.5's discussion of the Condorcet Jury Theorem are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and scientific claims, including 3× more tech-tree milestones, 2.3× more unique items and benefits from additional communication.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving belief correction, perspective-taking and cultural learning are unchanged. The same qualification that unprimed weak-agent collaboration can stagnate or deteriorate remains in Section 5.5.

D1.justification: V6 adds a direct MindForge GitHub repository link in the abstract; v5 refers to anonymized code in supplementary material without that project link. Implementation details, prompts, fine-tuning descriptions and model-provider information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section, bibliography and positioning relative to prior theory-of-mind, multi-agent and lifelong-learning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: V6 moves the NeurIPS checklist before Appendices A-G, adds an appendix title and appends a code-access sentence to the abstract. The scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract reflows, and the new appendix heading shifts the first appendix page's layout, including Tables 4-5. Appendix displays move with the reordered block; no figures or tables are added, removed or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: The direct repository link improves implementation discoverability compared with v5's generic reference to anonymized supplementary code. This is a limited documentation benefit; scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged, and the appendix/checklist rearrangement is largely neutral. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.
